VersionRange.union() loses an explicitly named pre-release when that literal also lies inside the other operand's bounds:

```python
from packaging.specifiers import SpecifierSet

ordinary = SpecifierSet(">=1,<2").to_range()
named = SpecifierSet("===1.5a1").to_range()
list((ordinary | named).filter(["1.5a1", "1.6"]))   # ['1.6'], expected ['1.5a1', '1.6']
list((named | ordinary).filter(["1.5a1", "1.6"]))   # same
```

Naming a pre-release literally (===1.5a1) opts it in when the literal lies outside the other range's bounds; it must also work when it lies inside them, in either union order. Details that must keep holding:
- the literal spelling matters: naming 1.5a1 does not admit the input string "1.5a01", and other pre-releases such as 1.5a2 stay excluded;
- an explicit pre-release policy still decides: with prereleases=False on both ranges no pre-release is admitted, with prereleases=True all are;
- the opt-in survives later narrowing, e.g. (ordinary | named) & (>=1.4) and (ordinary | named) - (>=1.7);
- a literal that was excluded (e.g. ordinary - named) does not become an opt-in when that result is united with ordinary bounds again.
